newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper names his 4th defense minister.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper names his 4th defense minister.

text.p: Embattled Colombian President Ernesto Samper appointed a new defence minister on Thursday, his fourth in two-and-a-half years in office.

Samper said Gilberto Echeverri Mejia, a respected 62-year-old business leader and chemical engineer from the northwestern province of Antioquia, had been appointed to replace Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez.
Gonzalez stepped down on Sunday after less than two months in office, two days after revealing that his congressional campaign accepted a $3,000 contribution from a reputed drug trafficker in 1989.

His predecessor, Juan Carlos Esguerra, was appointed ambassador to Washington in January and Samper's first defence minister, Fernando Botero, has been detained on drug corruption charges since August 1995.

The charges against Botero, son of the artist of the same name, stem from his high-level involvement in Samper's presidential campaign and its alleged receipt of millions of dollars in contributions from top drug lords.

Echeverri, a former Antioquia governor and member of the ruling Liberal Party, was minister of Economic Development under former president Julio Cesar Turbay Ayala. Even critics of the government welcomed his appointment.
"It's an excellent designation," said Sen. Juan Camilo Restrepo, a leader of the opposition Conservative Party. "He more than fulfils all the requirements."

Echeverri's appointment followed a surge in leftist guerrilla activity over the past year that has seriously embarrassed the thin-stretched military and left it looking increasingly unable to match the rebel challenge.

Samper alluded to this in a speech announcing Echeverri's appointment, saying he must be prepared "to combat without hesitation the various forms of violence that pose a true challenge to the survival of our democratic institutions."

But Samper also held out an olive branch to the guerrillas, saying the government would "continue seeking and trying out methods of reconciliation that would put an end to the long nightmare of confrontation that pursues us."
Echeverri has served on a regional peace group in Antioquia, one of the areas hardest hit by Colombia's more than three decades of guerrilla war and paramilitary violence.
